title: PARI hard-local portfolio and selector
objective: Profile #2510 and #1710 per prime across every complete local algorithm, implement a generic input-derived local strategy/cost improvement outside Round4, OM, BL, and fused analysis files, and preserve forced-path exact certificate equivalence

oracles: existing forced local algorithms and frozen canonical HNF certificates
PARI and Hecke direct timings from the durable performance receipt

handoff.summary: Profiles #2510 and #1710 across every complete local path, adds exact zero-root primary recognition and linear phi synthetic division, and supplies an inspectable feature-derived selector. #2510 factoring improves from about 2.53 ms to 0.34 ms on the measured host; exact selected and forced local lattices agree. The shared native Round-2 kernel remains the limiting boundary and the original <=2x/<=1.25 parity gates remain unmet.
risks: The selector cost scores are inspectable deterministic estimates, but they have not yet been calibrated across the complete 489-case standard corpus.
The new selector module is individually strict-Pyright clean but still needs the integration lane to add its path to pyrightconfig.json.
The isolated native #2510/#1710 ratios remain 7.98x and 4.66x versus the faster PARI/Hecke reference; this lane does not modify the shared native Round-2 kernel.
next_steps: Wire the selector into maximal_order_engine.py only after corpus-wide forced-path and ordinary-microcase calibration.

Use the recorded per-stage receipt to optimize the shared native Round-2 kernel for irregular #1710; benchmark a source-transparent polygon kernel before auto-selecting the regular #2510 path end to end.
